# Deferred Work Log

## Deferred from: code review of 9-5-installer-handoff-guide (2026-05-11)

- **DF1 — `is_outdated=False` when constraints provider unhydrated** [MEDIUM] [`src/open_ems/services/deployment_validation.py:206-212` — Story 9.4 surface] — `_current_config_version_safe()` returns `None` on `RuntimeError` (post-restart, pre-hydration); the `is_outdated` derivation returns `False` if `current_version is None`. During the hydration window after restart the "Download handoff guide" button is shown and the standalone route 200s even though the persisted result may be from a different `config_version`. Pre-existing semantic gap from Story 9.4; the validation page button visibility and route both inherit the bug. Resolution path: treat `current_version is None` as `is_outdated = True`, OR mirror the existing 503 pattern at `setup.py:773-776` and block the button/route when the provider is unavailable.
- **DF2 — Homeowner-rejection test for `/installer/handoff/guide` asserts status only, not redirect destination** [LOW] [`tests/unit/web/test_handoff_guide_route.py:435-443`] — `test_homeowner_rejected_on_handoff_guide` asserts `response.status_code == 302` without asserting the `Location` header points at the homeowner home. Other 302 tests in the same file DO assert redirect targets via `.endswith(...)`. A regression in `_ROLE_HOME["homeowner"]` would not be caught here. Test-tightening cosmetic; pick up during the next test-quality sweep.

## Carry-over sub-stories from: code review of 9-3 round 2 (2026-05-11)

_Six round-2 review findings each touch enough surface to deserve dedicated dev-cycle attention rather than in-session patches. Provisional names below; schedule between Story 9.4 and 9.5 OR as Epic 12-prep stories. All HIGH-severity items are listed first._

- **`9-Y-a-e2e-fail-abort-coverage` [HIGH — from R2P3]** [`tests/integration/web/test_setup_constraints_e2e.py::test_e2e_live_state_shift_aborts_activation_with_safety_fail`] — Existing test asserts 302 success with `peak_limit_kw=30` and 50 kW grid (AC7 WARN, not FAIL). The structural-FAIL abort path (`peak_limit_kw=0.4` < 0.5 kW threshold, OR capability lost between validate and activate) has no end-to-end coverage. Story scope: design a fixture that hits a real structural FAIL through the route, assert 400 + `validation_status='failed'` persisted + no `active_constraints` row written. Also rewrite the test name to match what it actually exercises (WARN path) OR replace its body. Acceptance: at least two new E2E tests covering FAIL-abort flows.
- **`9-Y-c-ev-window-form-ux` [MED — from R2P8]** [`src/open_ems/services/constraints.py:ConstraintDraftView` + `web/routes/setup.py:_form_view_from_request` + `_setup_constraints_form.html`] — Float fields preserve user raw via `raw_*_text` (P3 round 1); EV window does not. Invalid `<input type="time" value="25:99">` is silently emptied by most browsers. Empty-string sentinel makes "field omitted from form" indistinguishable from "explicitly cleared" → re-saving the form silently nulls a previously-set window. Pydantic non-paired-NULL model error with empty loc is routed to `ev_charging_window` slot unconditionally. Story scope: add `raw_ev_charging_window_start_text` / `_end_text` to `ConstraintDraftView`; inspect Pydantic error `type` before slot assignment; design sentinel for absent vs cleared field. Touches dataclass + route + template; needs design alignment on the absent-vs-cleared semantic.
- **`9-Y-d-migration-0011-populated-round-trip-and-idempotency` [MED — from R2P12]** [`migrations/versions/0011_add_constraint_configuration_tables.py` + `tests/integration/test_migrations.py`] — Round-trip test runs against empty DB; populated `active_constraints` with non-NULL EV window + non-empty `draft_constraints` row is unexercised on downgrade. Separately, re-running `upgrade head` on a DB already at 0011 fails with duplicate-column error. Story scope: extend round-trip test with populated-data variant; add column-existence guards to upgrade OR document non-idempotency in the migration docstring; consider running the test under both fresh and re-upgrade scenarios.
- **`9-Y-b-ac-and-r-artifact-narrative-sync` [MED — narrative — from R2P16]** [story spec file] — Bundle of contract-narrative drifts after P12/P13: AC6 step 8 ordering, AC6 "Idempotency" paragraph, AC7 grid_meter message text, AC8 confirmation `aria-label`, AC9 lifespan step number, R1 risk #3 case (b), R3 forbidden state #4, validation-template UX-component-#9-vs-#10 merge. Story scope: single coordinated edit to the AC + R-artifact text so the contract surface matches code. Pure narrative; no test changes; needs cross-checking against current code so each edit is true at time of writing.
- **`9-Y-e-bootstrap-activation-config-version-promote` [MED — from R2P20 / R2D2]** [`src/open_ems/storage/repositories/config_repo.py:_activate_locked` + `services/constraints.py`] — On first-ever activation when DB-seeded `active_constraints.config_version=0` matches the user's draft exactly, `activate()` raises `activate_called_with_no_changed_fields` and the installer cannot bootstrap. R2D2.A picked auto-promote semantics: short-circuit the `NoChangedFieldsError` guard when current `config_version == 0`; emit a synthetic audit row (`field='bootstrap'`, `previous_value=None`, `new_value={"config_version_promoted_from": 0}`) so the audit trail captures the bootstrap. Story scope: design audit semantics for empty-diff bootstrap; update `_build_audit_changes` OR add a dedicated bootstrap branch; add tests for the bootstrap path; verify existing "no audit row when no diff" tests still hold for non-bootstrap activations. Touches core invariants — needs deliberate test sweep.
- **`9-Y-f-peak-limit-upper-bound-and-migration-0013` [MED — from R2P21 / R2D3]** _Renumbered from `…-migration-0012` on 2026-05-11 because Story 9.4 owns migration `0012_add_deployment_validation_tables.py`._ [`src/open_ems/core/constraints.py` (`ActiveConstraintsInput`, `ActiveConstraints`, `ConstraintDraftInput`) + new migration 0013 + cascading test updates] — Per R2D3.A: add `Field(gt=0.0, le=63.0, allow_inf_nan=False)` to all three peak_limit_kw models; add a new migration 0013 with `CHECK (peak_limit_kw > 0 AND peak_limit_kw <= 63.0)` on `active_constraints.peak_limit_kw` and `draft_constraints.peak_limit_kw`; update spec-mandated AC7 schema-check error message to mention the 63 kW ceiling. Cascading test updates needed: `tests/unit/core/test_constraints.py:55` (peak_limit_kw=1000.0 asserts in-range — must move to assert-out-of-range), `tests/unit/engine/test_control_loop.py:189` (peak_limit_kw=99.0 — drop to ≤63 OR document why test uses out-of-band value). Story scope: bound + migration + test sweep + ensure no other code paths use peaks > 63.

## Deferred from: code review of 9-3-implement-constraint-configuration-with-staged-validation-and-single-increment-config-version (2026-05-11, round 2)

- **`assert_step_prerequisites` not called by `activate_draft` (duplicated inline)** [`src/open_ems/services/constraints.py:activate_draft` + `assert_step_prerequisites`] — P12 from round 1 explicitly allowed "keep both for defense in depth", so the inline duplication is not a bug. The single-source-of-truth refactor (have `activate_draft` call the shared helper) is a code-cleanliness improvement, not a correctness fix. Revisit during the next services-layer hygiene sweep.
- **`_changed_fields` and `_build_audit_changes` are two implementations of "what counts as changed"** [`src/open_ems/services/constraints.py:_changed_fields` + `storage/repositories/config_repo.py:_build_audit_changes`] — Both detect changes for the EV window correctly today (`None != None == False`), but they live in different modules with no cross-reference. A one-sided edit silently desyncs the structlog summary from the audit log. Consolidate to a single helper during a future refactor; add a test that asserts symmetry between the structlog `changed_fields` set and the `config_audit_log` row count for each activation.
- **Schema drift can poison a persisted draft permanently** [`src/open_ems/services/constraints.py:_check_schema`] — A future Pydantic input tightening (e.g. raising `peak_limit_kw` minimum, adding new model validators) makes previously-valid persisted drafts fail validation forever. The wizard offers no clear-draft action; the user has to manually re-edit every field. Address when the constraint schema gets its first breaking change — either via a draft-migration helper or by versioning the persisted draft.
- **`_check_capability_strategy` lock-free read; duplicate-role race window** [`src/open_ems/services/constraints.py:_check_capability_strategy`] — Reads `device_repo.list_all()` without a lock. Between the user's `/validate` click and the `/activate` click, an admin/peer session can reassign roles. The activation's re-validation inside the lock is authoritative (the activate decision is correct), but the report displayed to the user post-validate can mislead. No test asserts the consistency or documents the divergence. Resolve when device-role reassignment becomes multi-user concurrent.
- **Concurrent two POSTs in same session — lost update on draft** [`src/open_ems/services/constraints.py:upsert_draft`] — Two simultaneous POSTs from the same session (rare today — wizard is single-tab in practice) can overwrite each other's writes. Wizard is single-installer single-session in the contracted UX. Revisit when multi-tab or admin-shadow-edit workflows are added.
- **Float-equality in `_build_audit_changes` for `peak_limit_kw` and `battery_reserve_floor_percent`** [`src/open_ems/storage/repositories/config_repo.py:_build_audit_changes`] — Direct `!=` comparison; binary-identical-display-different floats (e.g. `0.1+0.2 != 0.3`) could produce phantom audit rows or hide real changes. `math.isclose` is the standard fix; defer to a future precision-hardening sweep.
- **Tampered DB row resilience** [`src/open_ems/storage/repositories/draft_constraints_repo.py:_row_to_draft` + `wizard_state_repo.py:_row_to_state` + `config_repo.py:get_active`] — `str(row[5])` bypasses the `Literal['pending','valid','failed']` annotation; corrupt JSON in `validation_report` propagates as JSONDecodeError; malformed ISO in `activated_at`/`created_at` raises generic ValueError with poor diagnostics; non-0/1 in `step_3_complete` integer column treated as truthy. CHECK constraints protect WRITES; READS from a tampered DB lack the same hardening. Defense-in-depth; not in 9.3 scope.
- **Lock-order documentation: write_lock → provider._lock; never reverse** [`src/open_ems/services/constraints.py:activate_draft` + `active_constraints.py:reload`] — `provider.reload()` is called inside the write lock and acquires its own internal lock. A future change that reverses the acquisition order would deadlock. Document the ordering invariant in the provider's docstring.
- **`set_step_3_complete_locked` updates `updated_at` even on idempotent retry** [`src/open_ems/storage/repositories/wizard_state_repo.py:set_step_3_complete_locked`] — Observability-only effect: idempotent re-call (no real state change) still bumps the `updated_at` timestamp, obscuring last-real-edit traceability. Adding `WHERE step_3_complete = 0` to the UPDATE prevents the churn but changes audit-log semantics; revisit when the wizard-state update model is reviewed holistically.
- **FAIL-persist exception coverage extends only to `ValueError`, not `IntegrityError` for FK CASCADE race** [`src/open_ems/services/constraints.py:activate_draft` step 5] — Continuation of round-1's W3 deferral. P14 catches the rowcount==0 `ValueError`; if aiosqlite surfaces the same CASCADE race as `IntegrityError` or `OperationalError`, the activation crashes with 500. Address when the storage-layer error mapping is centralized.
- **Validate POST info-leak: whether a draft exists is observable post-completion via differing rejection reasons** [`src/open_ems/web/routes/setup.py:post_validate_constraint_draft`] — A scripted caller (not the browser — GET handler short-circuits) can POST `/validate` after step_3_complete=1 and observe whether a draft happens to exist by which rejection reason fires (`step_3_already_complete` vs `draft_not_found_for_session`). Negligible disclosure.
- **`_in_txn_post_writes` callback's lock-hold duration could trigger SQLite OperationalError on contention** [`src/open_ems/storage/repositories/config_repo.py:_activate_locked`] — The atomic transaction now spans 4 tables and includes the callback's wizard-state UPDATE + draft DELETE. If contention forces a longer-than-expected lock hold, concurrent readers may see `database is locked` and HTMX clients may see 504. Document expected lock-hold duration; consider a timeout.
- **HH:MM validator inconsistencies** [`src/open_ems/core/constraints.py:_HH_MM_RE` + `_validate_hh_mm`] — `08:00`–`08:00` (equal start/end) is accepted; downstream policy may interpret as zero-duration vs 24-hour depending on consumer. Service layer strips whitespace; model layer's `fullmatch` rejects unstripped strings read from `active_constraints` text columns. Add a `start != end` validator OR document the equal-endpoint semantic; ensure strip-on-read consistency.
- **`ProviderNotReadyError` 503 missing `Retry-After` header** [`src/open_ems/web/routes/setup.py:get_constraints_page`] — Clients have no back-off signal; during startup, clients may hammer the endpoint and amplify the observability noise. Add `Retry-After: 5` in the next routes-hardening sweep.
- **Pydantic `errors[0]` non-dict edge — `first[0]` indexing on non-indexable raises IndexError** [`src/open_ems/services/constraints.py:_check_schema`] — Pydantic v2 internal shape is mostly stable; non-dict error objects are extremely rare. Defensive harden later.
- **AC10 partial: no unit test asserts `role="alert"` on populated validation-message div** [`tests/unit/web/test_setup_constraints_routes.py` + `_setup_constraints_form.html`] — AC8 a11y contract (`role="alert"` on populated validation message) has zero unit coverage; the placeholder a11y test is `xfail`. Add an assertion when the accessibility sweep is prioritized OR enable the xfailed placeholder test.
- **Wizard `_row_to_state` positional index shift after step_3 columns** [`src/open_ems/storage/repositories/wizard_state_repo.py:_row_to_state`] — Internal-only; the public SELECT was updated to match the new column order. If any legacy or out-of-tree code reads wizard_state by positional index (e.g. recovery scripts), it breaks silently. Document the column order invariant or use named columns.

## Deferred from: code review of 9-1-implement-device-discovery-step-with-live-probing-capability-classification-and-manual-entry (2026-05-11)

- **No delete-pending-entry route** [`src/open_ems/web/routes/setup.py` + `device_repo.py`] — Manual-entry probe crash before `mark_validated` leaves an orphan `validated=0` row. Story 9.1 repos are functionally correct but visually inconsistent with the 9.0b precedent. Refactor to the `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` pattern during a future storage-layer hardening sweep so all writers look the same.
- **OCPP synthesized address `f"/{cp_id}"`** [`src/open_ems/adapters/ocpp/central_system.py:115-122`] — Story 9.1's `OCPPRegisteredCharger.address` is the synthesized path, not the real WS mount. UI surfaces a misleading address; audit filters keyed on `address` cannot disambiguate from manual DSMR paths shaped `/...`. Revisit when OCPP wiring lands (Story 9.2/9.3) and the real WS mount path is available.
- **OCPP central_system is `None` in the lifespan** [`src/open_ems/web/app.py:311`] — `DeviceDiscoveryOrchestrator(ocpp_central_system=None, ...)`. If `device_registry` ever contains a row with `protocol="ocpp_1_6"`, the orchestrator never produces a matching `LiveDiscoveryRow` and the row classifies as NOT FOUND on every scan. Bounded today by AC5's OCPP-manual rejection and the absence of an `ocpp_self_registration` writer in 9.1, so no OCPP rows exist in practice. Surface as a 9.2 prerequisite when OCPP wiring is added.
- **Unshielded `adapter.close()` / `adapter.stop()` in `finally` blocks** [`src/open_ems/adapters/discovery.py:87-101, 187-188`] — Pre-existing in `adapters/discovery.py` (NOT introduced by 9.1). Address as a holistic adapter-layer pattern (`asyncio.shield`) during the next adapter hardening sweep.
- **`set_last_scan_id` race with admin-initiated session deletion → 500** [`src/open_ems/web/routes/setup.py:146` + `wizard_state_repo.py:1525-1527`] — Long-running scan completes after the installer's session was deleted by admin tooling; `set_last_scan_id` raises `ValueError("No wizard_state row...")` → uncaught 500 leaks DB internals to client. Narrow race in practice; harden when admin tooling for session management is built.
- **Manual-entry XSS-safety not asserted explicitly** [`src/open_ems/web/templates/installer/_setup_discovery_manual_form.html`] — Jinja autoescape protects today against `device_id=<script>`; no test asserts the rendered escape behavior. Add a regression test that submits a payload and asserts the response body does NOT contain the raw tag.
- **Cancellation e2e test exercises only one target** [`tests/integration/web/test_setup_discovery_e2e.py:2754-2769`] — `test_scan_cancellation_releases_resources` runs with a single Modbus target. Multi-target cancellation semantics (sibling tasks all receive `CancelledError`) are not exercised; standard asyncio behavior protects today but a future refactor of `_probe_*` could regress silently. Add a multi-target cancellation test.
- **CSRF middleware exhausts the request body via `await request.form()`** [`src/open_ems/web/csrf.py:71-79`] — Pre-existing pattern, not introduced by 9.1; Starlette's `BaseHTTPMiddleware` may decouple the FastAPI handler's view of the form from the middleware's cached view in some versions. Validate against the deployed Starlette version during a middleware-hardening sweep.
- **`_classify_not_found` reads the registry after probes complete** [`src/open_ems/services/device_discovery.py:313-336`] — A concurrent manual entry inserted between probe-fan-out and `list_all()` is included in the registry diff with no probe attempted. Single-installer race in practice; bounded by AC4's design. Snapshot the registry at scan start during a future orchestrator refactor.
- **`DiscoveryService` unbounded fan-out for large brownfield sites** [`src/open_ems/services/device_discovery.py:202-205` + `web/app.py:308`] — `DiscoveryService()` is constructed with no per-protocol concurrency cap. A site with 50+ Modbus devices serially-times-out into a multi-minute scan response. UX spec accepts 10s/30s per protocol but does not bound `N`. - **HTMX swap of `#scan-results-region` destroys forms inside it** [`src/open_ems/web/templates/installer/_scan_results.html:2031-2039`] — Retry-form inside the swapped region is GC'd mid-submission; focus moves to `body` element; screen-reader users lose context. A11y minor; refactor to swap a finer-grained region (per-row outerHTML) during a future UX polish pass.

- **`RoleConflict.device_ids` hash equality depends on `DeviceRepo.list_all()` ordering** [`src/open_ems/services/role_assignment.py:137`] — `RoleConflict` is `frozen=True` and hashed on `(role, device_ids: tuple[str, ...])`. The tuple ordering is taken from `list_all()` order; tests use `set(conflict.device_ids) == {...}` to avoid pinning. Any future change to `ORDER BY` in `list_all()` (e.g., adding `LIMIT`/`OFFSET` paging) changes the hash. Canonicalize via `tuple(sorted(device_ids))` at construction in a follow-up.
- **`RoleAssignmentService.evaluate_assignments` does a full `list_all()` + Pydantic-validate per request, twice on some routes** [`src/open_ems/services/role_assignment.py:122-166`] — `get_roles_page` and `post_assign_role` each call `evaluate_assignments` AND `evaluate_gate` (which itself calls `evaluate_assignments`), so two full passes per route call. Registry is bounded to a small-N residential install in v1, so this is not a real performance issue today; revisit if multi-site scale arrives or if the registry ever holds 100+ devices.
- **Spec AC3 enumerates `RoleGateOutcome` as 4 fields; implementation has 5** [`src/open_ems/services/role_assignment.py:107-115`] — The 5th field (`effective_acknowledged_gaps: frozenset[str]`) is consumed by `get_roles_page` and `post_advance_to_step_3` for AC6 step-4 staleness pruning — its existence is correct and necessary. Spec doc drift, not a code defect. Update Story 9.2 AC3's enumeration out-of-band so the contract surface matches the implementation.
- **Three definitions of `device_registry` / `wizard_state` schema (alembic migration + 2 test inlines)** [`tests/integration/web/test_setup_roles_e2e.py`, `tests/unit/web/test_setup_roles_routes.py`, `migrations/versions/0010_add_role_to_device_registry.py`] — Test fixtures re-declare the CREATE TABLE statements rather than running the alembic migration. Pre-existing pattern from Story 9.1 (inherits two definitions; 9.2 adds two more inlines). `test_migrations.py` asserts the alembic side only — drift between the migration and test schemas is now possible at four places. Refactor when storage-layer test harnesses are consolidated.
